messages.subject: JRI not getting object from R populated by data from query
messages.subject_clean: JRI not getting object from R populated by data from query
messages.body_plain:
I have an R script that retrieves data from a database, performs some
operations on it and provides me with data I want to retrive in Java using
JRI

beforeQuery <- c("Hello world")
query <- {{Query}}
....
queryResult <- fetch(queryResultSet,1)
The Java code that gets the result:

re.eval("source('" + location + "')"); //location of the R script
System.out.println(re.eval("beforeQuery").asString()); //works
System.out.println(re.eval("queryResult$column").asString()); //returns null
I have verified that queryResult is okay by running the R program
standalone.

What can I do to make sure that I can get the result inside the java
program successfully?

Regards,
Punit Jajodia

I investigated the issue further and found that any variable declared after
the database connection code isn't being obtained in java through JRI, even
when it isn't dependent on the query result.

testVar1 <- 1 # I am able to get this variable in java

library(RPostgreSQL)
drv<-dbDriver("PostgreSQL")
con<-dbConnect(drv,dbname="mydb",host="myhost",user="myuser",password="mypass")

testVar2 <- 1 # This one doesn't work

Regards,
Punit Jajodia

messages.subject_clean: JRI not getting object from R populated by data from query
messages.body_plain:
Turns out, the problem was that the RPostgreSQL package was installed in
the user's directory because I didn't specify the 'lib' parameter.

This worked when I ran the code from RStudio but gave an error while
running the same from within Java.

Moving the RPostgreSQL library folder to the location "C:\Program
Files\R\R-3.0.2\library"(the default location of the libraries) solved the
problem.

Thanks for all the guidance!

Regards,
Punit
